title: SvelteKit applications
description: For a SvelteKit application: private environment variables and server-only modules, server load functions for private data, the CSRF origin check and a Content Security Policy; builds on the svelte pack.

sources.title: SvelteKit docs, configuration: csrf and csp

rules.instruction: Read secrets only from SvelteKit's private environment module and only in server-only modules: a file with a `.server` segment in its name, a module in a `server` folder such as `src/lib/server/`, or a server load function. Never declare a secret as a public variable.
rules.verification: Check that each file the change adds that reads a secret is server-only, and that the build does not fail with SvelteKit's error on a server-only module imported into code that runs in the browser.

rules.instruction: Load data that needs a database, the file system or a private environment variable in a server load function (`+page.server.js`, `+layout.server.js`), not in a universal `+page.js`, which also runs in the browser.
rules.verification: Review each universal load function the change adds or edits and check that it calls no database and reads no private variable.

rules.instruction: Keep SvelteKit's CSRF protection on: do not set `csrf.checkOrigin` to `false`, and list in `csrf.trustedOrigins` only the origins that must submit forms to the application, never `'*'`.
rules.verification: task verify checks that no `svelte.config` file sets `checkOrigin: false` or trusts every origin; review any origin the change adds to `trustedOrigins`.

rules.instruction: Configure `kit.csp` in `svelte.config.js` (its `mode`, `directives` or `reportOnly`) so that SvelteKit sends a Content Security Policy with hashes or nonces for its own scripts and styles.
rules.verification: task verify checks that a `svelte.config` file declares `csp:`; also load a page of the built application and check the `Content-Security-Policy` or `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` header.
